chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with pending kidney transplantation and multiple cardiovascular/metabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient has a long-standing history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, obesity, tobacco use, and obstructive sleep apnea dating back to the 1940s-1950s. Prediabetes was diagnosed in the early 1970s and the patient is already receiving insulin therapy, suggesting progression toward overt diabetes. Diabetic kidney disease was documented in 1967 and has progressed sequentially through CKD stages 1‑4, with proteinuria and microalbuminuria noted. Anemia developed concurrently. The patient was placed on the kidney transplant waiting list in 1972. Current management includes a thiazide diuretic, low-dose statin, nicotine patch, and opioid‑containing analgesic, but lacks renoprotective agents (ACE‑I/ARB) and comprehensive blood pressure or renal function monitoring. Social factors include daily smoking, low educational attainment, a criminal record, and full‑time employment, all of which may affect adherence and transplant eligibility.

active_problems.name: Proteinuria due to type 2 diabetes mellitus
